rules.name: The Orange Means On Rule
rules.body: The app's accent marks the current, the active, the lit, and the focused, and nothing else: the shelf light, the current nav, the board's LEDs, focus, selection, the stats series. It never fills a surface, a button, or a heading. Orange inside an amp material is the head's own (Monolith's bar, Forge's rules), and belongs to it.

rules.name: The Materials Stay On Their Amps Rule
rules.body: An amp material appears as a full band, as an inner page's top band, or as that amp's mini on the shelf. Calm bands, doc sections, and components never borrow an amp's colors as accents.

rules.name: The Name Is The Display Rule
rules.body: Display scale belongs to the amp names. Statements, page titles, and headlines sit below it, and nothing sits above a heading as a label.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Geist sets everything except the two amps whose badges are script (Ember, Lantern), which get Fraunces. No third face. Comet's slant is a skew because Geist has no italic.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Numbers that get compared (tables, stat values, `.num`) use tabular figures.

rules.name: The Objects Cast, The Page Doesn't Rule
rules.body: Cards, buttons, tiles, notices and bands never get a shadow. When a surface needs separating, use a hairline.

dos: Do set every new surface on the ground, with hairlines for structure.
Do give an amp's content its own material band, with its tints for text and its re-inked buttons, and its real head from the app.
Do build materials from CSS gradients, the way the app builds its textures, with the grain on its own layer.
Do set an amp's name in its badge's lettering, at display scale, on one line.
Do keep one solid button per group, for the download that fits this computer.
Do put every motion behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, and use the shared ease (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`).
Do show measured numbers in ink at 500 inside dim copy, in tabular figures where they're compared.
Do follow the app: take the ground, panels, hairlines, inks and accent from src/ui/Theme.h, and the heads and screenshots from the test suite's proof.
donts: Don't use the orange for decoration, fills, headings, or buttons. It means on, active, or current.
Don't use an amp material outside its band, its inner-page band, or its mini.
Don't put a label or a number above a heading.
Don't use mockups, stock, or illustrations. Only the app's real snapshots and heads.
Don't shadow surfaces. Only heads and a lone featured screenshot cast a shadow, soft and straight down.
Don't add a third typeface or set body text in Fraunces.
Don't hide the download: the bar keeps its Download button at every width.

narrative.overview:
The app is a dark studio room with real gear in it. One amp head stands on a stage lit warmly from below. The pedals stand on a board under it in chain order, each in its own enclosure with an LED and a footswitch. The chrome around the gear (the top bar, the inspector, the scenes footer) is flat and quiet: near-black panels, 1px hairlines, Geist, grey inks. Everything that is on, selected, or active is lit in one orange, so from a step back the player reads the rig the way they'd read a real one: what's glowing is what's on.

The density is that of a working tool. Everything a player needs while playing fits on one fixed 1280 x 760 canvas: the preset and scene, which pedals are lit, the amp's knobs, the selected block's every control, and the eight scenes. The canvas scales uniformly to the window and letterboxes. The gear is the only thing with material, colour, and depth. The chrome never competes with it.

All of it is drawn in code. The heads, pedals, cab front, speaker, and markers are procedural art, rendered once per scale into a cache and blitted per frame. No bitmaps, no third-party trade dress, and no other company's product or amp names.
keyCharacteristics: A near-black ground (`bg`) with flat panels (`panel-bg`) and raised controls (`raised`), separated by 1px hairlines (`line1`).
One accent, orange (`accent`), meaning on, selected, or active. Red (`clip`) means a clip and nothing else.
Rendered gear in its own materials: nine amp heads, fifteen pedals, the cab's front, and the board's markers.
An off pedal is dimmed whole, so on and off read from two metres away.
Every knob in the inspector shows its value. Numbers are tabular.
Three short motions: the LED bloom, the scene glide, the stage crossfade.

rules.name: The Orange Means On Rule
rules.body: The accent marks what's on, selected, active, or being changed, and nothing else. It never fills a call to action: Record, Match, and Apply are primary buttons in the hairline colour, and they turn orange only while what they started is running.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red is a clip. Every other warning is a sentence in the neutral inks.

rules.name: The Gear Keeps Its Own Colours Rule
rules.body: Heads, pedals, the cab, the speaker, and the markers carry their own materials in their art files (`AmpHead.cpp`, `PedalArt.cpp`, `CabView.cpp`, `InspectorParts.cpp`, `Board.cpp`), not in Theme.h. An enclosure can be any colour (candy teal, seafoam, royal purple). What gear can't do is light up in any colour but the accent. LEDs, lamps, knob pointers, and value marks on gear are the accent or ink, never teal, emerald, or ice cyan.

rules.name: The No Hex In Components Rule
rules.body: Chrome components take every colour from `ui::theme` by name. Changing the chrome's look means changing Theme.h.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every number that changes live (knob values, Hz, ms, cents, CPU, BPM) uses tabular figures.

rules.name: The Read From A Step Back Rule
rules.body: Size goes where the player looks while playing: the preset name, the scene, the tuner's note, the lit scene. The rest of the chrome stays small.

rules.name: The Nothing Hidden Rule
rules.body: Preset, scene, the board's state, the amp's knobs, and the selected block's controls are all on one screen. Depth goes in the inspector's sections or an overlay. The board's tabs are the one place gear sits behind a tab, and only because every closed tab keeps an LED per block on the strip: what's on is never hidden.

rules.name: The Stage Follows The Selection Rule
rules.body: The amp's marker puts the stage on the amp and the cab's marker on the cab. An EQ pedal shows its graph and the next other pedal puts the stage back. Any other pedal leaves the stage where it is.

rules.name: The Gear Casts, The Chrome Doesn't Rule
rules.body: Panels, buttons, scenes, and overlays never get a shadow. Light and shadow come from the stage and the gear.

dos: **Do** take every chrome colour, type style, radius, and size from `src/ui/Theme.h` by name.
**Do** light what's on in the accent and dim what's off: a bypassed pedal at 55% brightness and 45% saturation, its LED the dead lens.
**Do** draw new gear procedurally, cache it per scale, and draw its state (LED, rings, dimming) without re-rendering.
**Do** give every inspector knob its value under its caption, in tabular figures.
**Do** follow the inspector grammar for a new block: header, meter, mode, large knobs, then sections.
**Do** keep motion to the three tokens (`ledGlowSeconds` 0.35, `sceneGlideSeconds` 0.16, `stageFadeSeconds` 0.18) and let snapshots finish it.
**Do** say warnings in words, in the neutral inks.
donts: **Don't** fill a call to action with orange; use the primary button.
**Don't** use red for anything but a clip.
**Don't** let a light on gear (an LED, lamp, pointer, or value mark) take any colour but the accent or ink.
**Don't** shadow chrome panels, buttons, or scenes.
**Don't** put a value arc on the head's gear knobs; arcs belong to the inspector.
**Don't** use another company's product or amp names, or their art or trade dress.
